v.1: Woe to the defrauders, who use short measures,
v.2: who, when they measure [a commodity bought] from the people, take the full measure,
v.3: but diminish when they measure or weigh for them.
v.4: Do they not know that they will be resurrected
v.6: a day when mankind will stand before the Lord of all the worlds?
v.7: Indeed, the record of the vicious is in Sijjeen.
v.8: And what will show you what is Sijjeen?
v.10: Woe to the deniers on that day,
v.11: who deny the Day of Retribution;
v.12: and none denies it except every sinful transgressor.
v.13: When Our signs are recited to him, he says, ‘Myths of the ancients!’
v.14: No, that is not the case! Rather, their hearts have been sullied by what they have been earning.
v.15: Indeed, they will be alienated from their Lord on that day.
v.17: then told, ‘This is what you used to deny!’
v.18: Indeed, the record of the pious is in Illeeyun.
v.19: And what will show you what is Illeeyun?
v.21: witnessed by those brought near [to Allah].
v.22: The pious shall be amid bliss,
v.24: You will perceive in their faces the freshness of bliss.
v.25: They will be served with a sealed pure wine,
v.26: whose seal is musk—for such let the viers vie—
v.27: and whose seasoning is from Tasneem,
v.28: a spring where those brought near [to Allah] drink.
v.29: Indeed the guilty used to laugh at the faithful,
v.30: and when they passed them by they would wink at each other,
v.31: and when they returned to their folks they would return amused,
v.32: and when they saw them they would say, ‘Indeed those are the astray!’
v.33: Though they were not sent to watch over them.
v.34: So today the faithful will laugh at the faithless,
v.36: Have the faithless been requited for what they used to do?
